newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Dec 13.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 27.43 percent rise in turnover in week to December 13 and traders attributed the increase to slightly improved market liquidity.
Total turnover rose to 32.39 million dinars ($6.35 million) from 25.417 million dinars a week ago. The number of deals declined to 161 from 184, the bourse said.

"Cyclical up-and-down changes in the BSE turnover continue. There was a little more money on the market, but this week again we expect subdued activity because pensions are paid out," a trader told Reuters.

Traders said the market discounted a slide in the dinar black market rate to 3.7 to the German mark as a reaction to four weeks of opposition and student protests accusing the ruling Socialists of election fraud.
"There is no money in the banking sector which could push the dinar rate down. Banks are no longer market makers on the black market," another trader said.
For the week ending December 13, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper again dominated the BSE turnover with 132 deals worth 16.695 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded 24 times for a volume of 2.945 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 220.88 and 793 percent.
Traders said average annual interest rates hovered around 417 percent or 0.45 a day.
* BSE reported one deal in the central bank short-term bonds worth 12 million dinars.
* There was no trade in the wheat forward contracts.

"The sale of those contracts has just begun and it will last until February 7. Right now there is no buyer interest because flour mills and bakeries have no money. But activity will pick up ahead of the sale deadline," a trader said.
